newsitem.title: UK: Brent sees three cargoes trade at varying levels.
newsitem.headline: Brent sees three cargoes trade at varying levels.

text.p: North Sea crude markets focused on Dated Brent on Tuesday with three physical deals reported at varying levels, traders said.

A November 21-23 cargo was bought by a major oil company at December -44 cents. This major now holds some 4-5 November Brent cargoes. A November 20-22 cargo then moved at December -48 cents, sold by a Wall Street refiner who has been very active in the market this week.
The same Wall Street refiner then bought a November 24-26 cargo from an equity holder at December -49 cents.

Talk that one million barrels of Brent has been sold to a U.S. refiner for mid-December arrival could not be confirmed, but traders predicted a sharp drop in Dated Brent levels, should a VLCC of November crude not move out of Europe.
"We need at least one VLCC to move out of the area. If it doesn't, this market could be in serious trouble and we will see the weakness running into December," one refiner said.
Brent and Forties loading programmes for December, due out later this week, are expected to be higher than November, traders said.
"There's no maintenance and an extra day in the month. They could be quite chunky programmes," one said.
Brent paper markets saw just one deal -- a Dec/Jan trading at +32 cents. Both intermonths and CFDs were well offered, looking for buyers.
In the Mediterranean, Urals still offered refiners better netbacks than other sour grades, traders said.
"Urals is the best. The (refining) margin is 40 cents (a barrel) better than Syrian Light and 10 or 15 cents better than Iran Heavy," said one Italian refiner.
